chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

That Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was raised to him a case of a man who killed a pig, so he made him responsible for its price, and a case was raised to him of a man who broke a guitar, so he dismissed it.

key_terms.بَرْبَط: A type of lute or musical instrument

ai.seo_question: What was the judicial ruling of Imam Ali regarding killing a pig versus breaking a musical instrument?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates Imam Ali’s (AS) judicial discretion (*ijtihad*) in distinguishing between the intrinsic value of an animal and the functional utility of an object. By imposing financial compensation for the pig, which was considered a valuable commodity in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabia, while dismissing the case for the broken *barbat* (lute), he highlights the principle that penalties are tied to specific legal damages rather than mere destruction. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on contextual jurisprudence, where the social and economic status of the item determines the severity of the *diya* or compensation.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

that Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>, a matter was raised to him<sup>asws</sup> of a man who killed a pig, so he<sup>asws</sup> made him responsible for its price, and a matter was raised to him<sup>asws</sup> of a man who had broken a guitar (musical instrument), so he<sup>asws</sup> invalidated it (dismissed the case)’.
